column1: Read First
I would recommend watching my video tutorial series to gain an understanding of how to learn these algs (work in progress) -->
This list is designed for people learning 3-Style algs for the first time
This list uses the UFR buffer for corners and UF buffer for edges
I use the Speffz lettering scheme here to label algs (e.g. using 'BA' instead of 'URB UBL')
About the Algs
This algs in this list requires you to have an understanding of how commutators work
All algs are in commutator notation [S: [A, B]] is S A B A' B' S' (' represents the inverse)
You should learn the inverse of every alg, which would be [S: B, A]]
The 3-cycle [Buffer (C) > X > Y > Buffer (C)] is represented by XY
The way I notate the algs is based on what I think best represents the way in which you fingertrick it
How to Learn/Tips on Learning
The approach I would recommend would be to learn with a sticker by sticker approach
A starting point in terms of learning pace would be to spend an hour or so learning a sticker every day
The list is designed so you can easily import the algs into a flashcards app/website to learn the algs
Your end goal is to be able to recall all of these algs with as little effort as possible
Always look out for and note similarities/connections to other algs while learning
You can download this spreadsheet and customise your letter scheme under the 'Letter Scheme' sheet
I'd recommend using the parity algs as a placeholder while learning corners and Orozco while learning edges
Recommended Progression
Switch to CEEC order
Switch to C (UFR) as your corner buffer and learn all of the parity algs
Learn all corner algs
Switch to C (UF) as your edge buffer, learn Q comms and then learn Orozco
Learn all edge algs
